facts.statement: Tendaguripterus lived during the Late Kimmeridgian to Early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Kimmeridgian to Early Tithonian, Late Jurassic

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Tendaguripterus is a single dentary (lower jaw) found in the Tendaguru Formation in southeastern Lindi, Tanzania.
facts.quote: The only specimen – a dentary (lower jaw) – was discovered in strata of the Tendaguru Formation in southeastern Lindi.

facts.statement: German fossil collectors discovered the specimen between 1910 and 1912 at Site Jg during an expedition to the Tendaguru Formation.
facts.quote: Between 1910 and 1912, members of a German fossil expedition to the Tendaguru Formation in then-German East Africa collected many pterosaur fossils from Site Jg.

facts.statement: Paleontologists David Unwin and Wolf-Dieter Heinrich formally described the fossil as a new genus and species in 1999.
facts.quote: This specimen was unnoticed for decades until in 1999, paleontologists David Unwin and Wolf-Dieter Heinrich scientifically described it as belonging to a new genus and species of pterosaur.

facts.statement: The species was named Tendaguripterus recki in honor of the German geologist Hans Reck.
facts.quote: They named it Tendaguripterus recki, the only known species, after German geologist Hans Reck.

facts.statement: The preserved dentary is short, robust, and tall, containing four tooth sockets and two incomplete teeth.
facts.quote: The dentary is short, robust, and tall, with four alveoli (tooth sockets) and two incomplete teeth preserved.

facts.statement: The lower jaw becomes over 1.5 times deeper at the back than at the front, creating an extremely deep shape.
facts.quote: Going posteriorly (towards the back), the dentary becomes over 1.5 times the height of the anterior (front) end, creating an extremely deep shape.

facts.statement: Researchers have proposed that Tendaguripterus was a durophage that fed on hard-shelled invertebrates like bivalves.
facts.quote: It has been proposed that Tendaguripterus was durophagus, feeding on hard invertebrates like bivalves.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with Germanodactylus, the wingspan of Tendaguripterus is estimated to be about 1 meter wide.
facts.quote: Based on Germanodactylus, its wingspan was about 1 m wide.

facts.statement: Specimen MB.R.1290 serves as the holotype and is the only known fossil of Tendaguripterus.
facts.quote: MB.R.1290 was selected as the holotype (name-bearing) specimen and remains the only fossil reported of Tendaguripterus.

facts.statement: The genus name combines "Tendaguru", the location of discovery, and the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The generic name comes from "Tendaguru", where the fossil was collected, and the Greek word ptero meaning "wing".

facts.statement: In 1999, Unwin and Heinrich estimated the complete skull length at 20 cm and the wingspan at 1 meter.
facts.quote: In 1999, Unwin and Heinrich stated the skull of Tendaguripterus was around 20 cm when complete based on Germanodactylus, with an estimated wingspan width of 1 m.

facts.statement: The preserved jaw fragment measures 25.9 cm in length and is 9.9 cm deep at its deepest point near the back.
facts.quote: MB.R.1290 has a preserved length of 25.9 cm and is dorsoventrally (top-bottom) deepest towards the posterior (back) end, at 9.9 cm deep.

facts.statement: Unlike other dsungaripteroids, the teeth of Tendaguripterus project backward rather than upward or forward.
facts.quote: Unlike any other dsungaripteroids, Tendaguripterus' teeth project posteriorly instead of vertically or anteriorly.

facts.statement: In 2007, Alexander Kellner and colleagues argued that the resemblance between Tendaguripterus and other dsungaripteroids was superficial.
facts.quote: However, in a 2007 study Brazilian paleontologist Alexander Kellner and colleagues stated that its resemblance to Germanodactylus and Dsungaripterus was superficial.

facts.statement: Kellner and colleagues noted that Tendaguripterus lacks definitive traits of Dsungaripteroidea and cannot be confirmed as a pterodactyloid.
facts.quote: The authors added by noting Tendaguripterus cannot even definitively be considered a pterodactyloid and that it lacked any synapomorphies of Dsungaripteroidea.

facts.statement: Kellner and colleagues established the new family Tendaguripteridae to contain Tendaguripterus exclusively.
facts.quote: As a result, they named a new family, Tendaguripteridae, exclusively for the genus.

facts.statement: It remains unclear whether Tendaguripterus belongs to Dsungaripteroidea or another group, as it has not been included in recent phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: Since its description, Tendaguripterus has not been included in a phylogenetic analysis. Its affinities remain unclear.

facts.statement: Tendaguripterus lived alongside dinosaurs such as Giraffatitan and Kentrosaurus, as well as other pterosaurs like Rhamphorhynchus and Pterodactylus.
facts.quote: Here it coexisted with other pterosaurs like "Rhamphorhynchus" tendagurensis and "Pterodactylus" brancai and dinosaurs like Giraffatitan and Kentrosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Tendaguripterus likely ate bivalves and other hard-shelled invertebrates.
facts.quote: Tendaguripterus may have consumed bivalves and other hard-shelled invertebrates.

facts.statement: Tendaguripterus fossils come from the Late Jurassic Tendaguru Formation in southeastern Tanzania.
facts.quote: The Tendaguru Formation is a Late Jurassic-aged geologic formation in the Mandawa Basin in southeastern Tanzania.

facts.statement: Tendaguripterus lived specifically during the late Kimmeridgian age within the Middle Saurian Member of the formation.
facts.quote: Tendaguripterus is exclusive to the late Kimmeridgian-aged Middle Saurian Member.

facts.statement: The ecosystem where Tendaguripterus lived included shallow marine lagoons, tidal flats, and vegetated inland areas.
facts.quote: The Tendaguru ecosystem primarily consisted of three types of environment: shallow, lagoon-like marine environments, tidal flats and low coastal environments; and vegetated inland environments.

facts.statement: Fossil material of Tendaguripterus was collected during German expeditions between 1909 and 1913 and identified by Hans Reck in 1931.
facts.quote: Durante las expediciones paleontológicas alemanas al África Oriental Alemana entre 1909 y 1913, algún material fósil de pterosaurio fue recolectado y reconocido como tal por Hans Reck en 1931.

facts.statement: The genus Tendaguripterus was named in 1999 by David Unwin and Wolf-Dieter Heinrich.
facts.quote: En 1999 David Unwin y Wolf-Dieter Heinrich nombraron un nuevo género para éste.

facts.statement: The genus is based on the holotype MB.R.1290, which is a tooth-bearing mandible.
facts.quote: El género está basado en el holotipo MB.R.1290, una mandíbula con diente (la región sinfiseal, donde ambas mitades de la mandíbula se encuentran y fusionan en un solo elemento).

facts.statement: The teeth in the posterior section of the fossil fragment point significantly backward.
facts.quote: Los dientes en la sección posterior del fragmento apunta bastante hacia atrás.

facts.statement: In 2007, Alexander Kellner argued that Tendaguripterus's resemblance to Germanodactylus and Dsungaripterus was superficial and that it might not belong to Pterodactyloidea but rather be a more basal pterosaur.
facts.quote: En 2007 Alexander Kellner estableció que su parecido tanto a Germanodactylus como a Dsungaripterus era superficial y que ni siquiera había certeza de que fuera un miembro de los Pterodactyloidea, en vez de ser un pterosaurio más basal.

facts.statement: Based on Kellner's analysis, Tendaguripterus is placed in the undefined clade Tendaguripteridae, of which it is the only known member.
facts.quote: De acuerdo a esto él lo refirió a un nuevo clado indefinido, los Tendaguripteridae, del cual es el único representante.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Tendaguripterus is Unwin & Heinrich, 1999.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Unwin & Heinrich, 1999

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Tendaguripterus recki.
facts.quote: type_species: T. recki

facts.statement: Tendaguripterus was originally considered a member of the family Germanodactylidae.
facts.quote: familia: Germanodactylidae

facts.statement: Tendaguripterus is classified within the superfamily Dsungaripteroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Dsungaripteroidea

facts.statement: Tendaguripterus lived between 152.21 and 149.2 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Tendaguripterus was likely a small pterosaur with an estimated skull length of 20 centimeters and a wingspan of nearly 100 centimeters.
rejected.quote: En general, este pudo haber sido un pterosaurio pequeño; la longitud craneal se ha estimado en veinte centímetros, y la envergadura en cerca de 100 centímetros.
